Chapter 14 of 19

The Sunset

ReceiveWestern horizon / citywide140 BPM
The story

In Terminal City, sunset is not a view. It is a procedure. The crows are already home. The Wire Choir turns itself down by an amount nobody can measure. And on the western horizon the light goes out the way a machine winds down at the end of a shift.

In that minute, the day signs the city over to the night. The Sixth Hour is authorised. The Nocturnals are released. Whatever the day could not use begins its slow walk toward the Eternal Night. Nothing changes hands until the sun is fully down, which is why everything in the city seems to pause and wait for it.

People stop on the seawall and on rooftops to watch. This is correct. Of all the parts of the daily cycle, the Sunset is the only one designed to be seen. Last light. Turn the key. The other city is clocking in.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
